input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification, or records-examination right exercisable by Kubient against AP. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verify" return no hits, and a full read of the single section confirms the point: the fees provision (p0023) is a pure revenue-share with sequential liability and imposes no obligation on AP to open books or systems for verification, and no compliance or use-of-service provision (p0024-p0025) grants Kubient examination rights. The only access obligation binding AP is in p0001, which is limited to "access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services" — that is forward-looking delivery cooperation tied to performance, not a verification or audit right, and it carries no inspection, frequency, cost, or system-access consequence. Because there is no audit right binding our party, the AUDIT walk-away risks (unlimited/unannounced audits or remote access to AP systems) are absent and the preferred position's frequency, notice, independent-auditor, cost-shifting and no-system-access limits have nothing to attach to. Adding audit machinery here would only create an audit right that does not currently exist, which is worse for AP than silence, so no redline is proposed. (Separately, note that Impressions are "measured by Kubient" under p0009 with no AP verification right — a customer-favorable audit right over Kubient would be a distinct ask outside this rule's scope.)
